title: Quick Revision: Structure of the Atom

bullets: **Thomson:** a positive sphere with electrons embedded in it, like seeds in a watermelon. Atom is neutral overall.

**Rutherford (α-particle scattering on gold foil):** most α-particles passed straight through, so most of the atom is **empty space**; a few were deflected and very few bounced back, so the positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny **nucleus**.
**Drawback of Rutherford's model:** a revolving electron should lose energy and fall into the nucleus, so the atom would be unstable.
**Bohr:** electrons revolve in certain discrete orbits (shells K, L, M, N) and do not radiate energy while in them.

box: Atomic number Z = number of protons · Mass number A = protons + neutrons · Neutrons = A − Z
Maximum electrons in a shell = 2n^{2}: K = 2, L = 8, M = 18 (but the outermost shell holds at most 8)
**Valency** = electrons gained, lost or shared to complete the octet, e.g. Na (2, 8, 1): 1; Cl (2, 8, 7): 1; O (2, 6): 2

bullets: **Isotopes:** same atomic number, different mass number, e.g. hydrogen-1, 2, 3; carbon-12 and carbon-14. Uses: uranium-235 as nuclear fuel, cobalt-60 to treat cancer, iodine-131 to treat goitre.
**Isobars:** same mass number, different atomic number, e.g. calcium-40 and argon-40.

blocks.p: 1. Write the electronic configuration of sulphur (Z = 16) and give its valency.
2. An atom has 11 protons and 12 neutrons. Find its atomic number and mass number.
